clue.text: Mean little woman longing to keep child in

parts.note: Penny is a woman's name, a pet form of Penelope

indicators.note: the longing word holds the child abbreviation within it, keeping it in

parts.note: longing means pining

explanation.surface: A small woman's yearning to keep her child at home is described as mean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to keep ... in' is split around 'child': the longing word wraps the child abbreviation. 'Little woman' is just a girl's name, not a hint at size.
explanation.definitionFit: Being miserly with every coin is to be stingy, a synonym of mean.

clue.text: A prof's pal tries to work out hard material

indicators.note: to work out the words means to solve them, here rearranging their letters

explanation.surface: An academic's friend struggles to understand some tough substance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to work out' rearranges A PROFS PAL TRIES.
explanation.definitionFit: The gypsum paste sets into a solid used for casts and moulds, a hard substance.

clue.text: Drink up — to queen and country!

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: gin is a drink
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the queen

explanation.surface: A toast: drink up to the monarch and the nation!
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reads the drink from the bottom; the toast in the surface hides that 'queen' is the royal cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: The West African nation named after its river is a country.

clue.text: Cowardly character gets a warning from the ref

parts.note: yellow means cowardly
a card is an eccentric or amusing person, a character

explanation.surface: A timid player is cautioned by the referee.
explanation.definitionFit: In football the referee shows a cautioning signal to a player for a foul.

clue.text: I am at home sheltering little girl from wicked African dictator

indicators.note: the girl's name is held within the other words, sheltered by them

parts.note: taken as written
Di is a short form of Diana, a little name for a girl
in means at home

explanation.surface: A man protects a young girl from a cruel African tyrant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sheltering' places the little girl just after the opening I, inside the rest of the phrase; the surface 'from' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Uganda's ruler in the 1970s was a brutal military dictator in Africa.

clue.text: Stuck together in this place tucking into the fish

indicators.note: the place word goes inside the fish word, tucking into it

parts.note: cod is a fish
here means in this place

explanation.surface: Food is stuck together where someone is eating the fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' looks like eating the fish, but it is a container signal: the place word goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that stuck together held as one, which is a synonym.

clue.text: Tablets lacking power? These may remain

definitions.text: Tablets lacking power? These may remain

indicators.note: lacking says the power letter is missing from the tablets word

parts.note: pills are tablets
P is the symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: Weak medicine leaves the patient's complaints untreated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' takes P out of PILLS. The whole clue also defines: if the tablets have no strength, the ailments stay.
explanation.definitionFit: Ailments and troubles persist when medicine is too weak to cure them.

clue.text: Irritated if one is imprisoned — or pleased?

indicators.note: the if and one pieces are locked inside the irritated word

parts.note: grated means irritated
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Would someone be annoyed or happy if locked up?
explanation.walkthrough: 'is imprisoned' locks the two short pieces inside the irritated word; the question mark covers the oddity of being both cross and glad.
explanation.definitionFit: Being satisfied and gladdened is a synonym for being pleased.

clue.text: He's a camper seen cooking food

indicators.note: cooking means the words are mixed up like ingredients

explanation.surface: A man on a camping trip is spotted making a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' rearranges HES A CAMPER SEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard Italian grating staple is an example of food.

clue.text: One swims, undoing flesh gain!

indicators.note: undoing the words flesh gain unpicks their letters so they can be rearranged

explanation.surface: A dieter laments that putting on weight is their downfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undoing' rearranges the letters of FLESH GAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: This tropical fish is a creature that swims, so the definition describes it by an example of its behaviour.

clue.text: Animal a Buddhist priest mentioned

indicators.note: mentioned means spoken, so the priest's title is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist monk or priest

explanation.surface: Someone names an animal and a Buddhist priest in the same breath.
explanation.walkthrough: LAMA and the South American pack beast sound the same but the beast takes a double L.
explanation.definitionFit: The Andean pack beast is a domesticated mammal, an example of an animal.

clue.text: Trunk and roots destroyed

indicators.note: destroyed tells us the word roots is broken up and its letters rebuilt

explanation.surface: A tree's trunk and roots have been wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyed' rearranges ROOTS. The tree picture makes 'Trunk' look botanical, but it is the body.
explanation.definitionFit: The human body without head and limbs is called the trunk, a synonym.

clue.text: Month to vote for communist

parts.note: Mar is the short form of March
a cross on a ballot paper marks a vote for a candidate

explanation.surface: A month in which to vote for a communist candidate.
explanation.definitionFit: Karl the German philosopher founded communist theory, so he is the archetypal communist.

clue.text: Old country master is bowled over

indicators.note: bowled over means knocked head over heels, so both words are turned backwards

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a master's degree

explanation.surface: A teacher from an old country is overwhelmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowled over' is a cricket image but signals one reversal of the degree and 'is' together; the result is the old name for Thailand.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the former name of Thailand until 1939, so it is a country of old.

clue.text: Not one of the cathedral's big guns from what we hear

definitions.text: Not one of the cathedral's big guns from what we hear

parts.words: Not one of the cathedral's big guns from what we hear
parts.note: a junior cleric of a cathedral sounds like a small artillery piece, so he is no big gun in either sense

explanation.surface: Someone hears that a certain clergyman lacks influence at the cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: A canon is a cathedral clergyman; spoken aloud, his junior title sounds like a lesser cannon, the opposite of a big gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A junior cleric attached to a cathedral is not among its senior dignitaries.

clue.text: Polish religious image showing Italian flower

parts.note: to polish is to rub
an icon is a holy painting in the Orthodox church

explanation.surface: Polishing a religious painting that depicts an Italian bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' here is 'something that flows', a crossword favourite for a river; this is the stream Caesar crossed.
explanation.definitionFit: The stream crossed by Caesar in 49 BC is in northern Italy, and in crosswords a river is a thing that flows.

clue.text: Many bones will get broken? Certainly not!

indicators.note: the bones are broken, so their letters are smashed and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asked if many bones will break replies firmly no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will get broken' rearranges MANY BONES.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an emphatic refusal, meaning not at all.

clue.text: Rags for the cleaners?

parts.note: rags are scornful slang for newspapers, and cleaners who come in each day share the same plural name as papers printed each day

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether these old cloths are meant for the cleaning staff.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests dusters; in fact it describes newspapers ('rags') and daily household helps ('the cleaners') with one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Papers published every day and charwomen hired by the day are both known by this plural noun.

clue.text: Enjoyable time had by novice in religious ceremony

parts.note: enjoyable as a description can be fun
an era is a period of time
L is a learner, as on the L-plate of a learner driver

explanation.surface: A newcomer has a good time during a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: A burial service for the dead is a solemn rite, often held in church.

clue.text: Match is this — not going well? Look black

definitions.text: Match is this — not going well?

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look
sable is black in heraldry

explanation.surface: A team in trouble looks gloomy as the match goes badly.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: a game going badly is one that could be lost.
explanation.definitionFit: A game going badly is one that might be lost, which is what the adjective means.

clue.text: Battle sees 50 odd invading boggy area

indicators.note: the fifty and odd pieces push into the marsh word, invading it

parts.note: a fen is low-lying marshland
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
taken as written

explanation.surface: A battle in which fifty strange soldiers storm a marsh.
explanation.walkthrough: FLODDEN was a battle of 1513 in which the English defeated the Scots in Northumberland.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1513 English victory over James IV of Scotland is the clash named here.

clue.text: One part of the anatomy or another brought into class

indicators.note: the or and another pieces are placed inside the class word

parts.note: a form is a school class
another part of the anatomy, here the ear

explanation.surface: Body parts are brought into a biology lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' stands for a second body part; 'brought into' puts it, with 'or', inside the school class.
explanation.definitionFit: The arm between elbow and wrist is a part of the body.

clue.text: Top position achieved by bill and yours truly

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill to be settled
yours truly is a jokey way of saying me

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of reaching the top together with a man called Bill.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest point or peak of something is its summit.

clue.text: Ruler from south Africa received by turkey

indicators.note: the south and Africa letters are taken into the turkey abbreviation, received by it

parts.note: TR is the international vehicle registration code for Turkey
A can stand for Africa

explanation.surface: A ruler from southern Africa is welcomed by Turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian emperor was an absolute monarch, a kind of ruler.

clue.text: About to get impetuous? Accident could result

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
impetuous and rash both mean acting without thought

explanation.surface: Being reckless at the wheel could lead to an accident.
explanation.definitionFit: A collision of vehicles is a common kind of accident.

clue.text: Great north road — vehicle's collected mites and ticks

indicators.note: the vehicle is picked up by the road, collected inside it

parts.note: the Great North Road is the A1 from London to Edinburgh, with 1 read as I
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A car on the A1 has gathered creepy-crawlies.
explanation.walkthrough: The Great North Road is Britain's A1 from London to Scotland; its 1 doubles as the letter I, and 'collected' puts CAR inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The zoological order of small arachnids takes in both mites and ticks.

clue.text: Stars not all highly rated

indicators.note: not all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Not every celebrity is well thought of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stars' looks like celebrities but is a constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: The northern constellation containing Vega is a group of stars.

clue.text: I agree one of the lecturers should leave the country

indicators.note: one letter is told to leave the agreeing word, so it is removed

parts.note: to tally is to agree or match up
L is short for lecturer, one of the double L in the agreeing word

explanation.surface: Someone agrees one of the academic staff should emigrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'should leave' removes just one of the two Ls in the agreeing word; the surface has an academic emigrating.
explanation.definitionFit: This European nation of the boot-shaped peninsula is a country.

clue.text: Great idea from supporter at home on western avenue

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
in means at home

explanation.surface: An inspiration from a fan who lives on a westerly street.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden clever thought is an inspired notion, a synonym.

clue.text: As a retired politician could be preparing a kitten's meals

definitions.text: As a retired politician could be

indicators.note: preparing suggests the words are worked on and rearranged like ingredients

explanation.surface: Someone notes how dignified a retired politician looks while fixing the cat's dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'preparing' rearranges the letters of A KITTENS MEALS.
explanation.definitionFit: An elder politician often acts with dignity and wisdom, the qualities the adjective describes.
